issues.description: The problem statement and template expect concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (and tasks reference these exact class names), but the solution repository implements classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat instead (while Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java in the solution are empty). This name mismatch between the expected class identifiers and the solution classes is structural: students following the specification and template will implement/instantiate Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the provided solution uses different class names, which is confusing and prevents direct correspondence between the solution and the exercise specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution repository use the same concrete class names as the problem specification and template. Rename SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, and Goat respectively (updating their class declarations and filenames), or add thin wrapper classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat that delegate to the Space* implementations. Ensure Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java contain the intended implementations so the solution, template, and problem statement consistently refer to the same class names.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the solution implementation provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. This mismatch means students mapping the requirement (implement Seal/Pig/Goat) to the provided solution artifacts will encounter different class identifiers and may be confused when looking for expected classes or when the song/printing uses getSimpleName() (which will print the 'Space' prefixed names).
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent class names across artifacts. Rename SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat in the solution to Seal, Pig, and Goat (or add thin wrapper classes with the expected names delegating to the Space* classes). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use the Space-prefixed names — pick one naming scheme and apply it consistently.
